lesson.title: The Preterite: The Dot in Time
lesson.subtitle: hablé, comí, fue — completed single past events bounded in time

hook.title: One Word for a Completed Dot on the Timeline
hook.content: When an action happened at a closed, finished point in the past — like ayer ('yesterday'), anoche ('last night'), or el lunes pasado ('last Monday') — Spanish uses a crisp one-word past tense called the Preterite (el pretérito indefinido). For -ar verbs, 'I [verb]-ed' ends in stressed -é (hablé 'I spoke', visité 'I visited') and 'he/she/usted [verb]-ed' ends in stressed -ó (habló 'he/she spoke', visitó 'he/she visited'). For -er and -ir verbs, 'I [verb]-ed' ends in stressed -í (comí 'I ate', viví 'I lived') and 3rd person ends in -ió (comió, vivió)!

pattern.title: How One Accent Mark Separates Present from Past!
pattern.content: Look at the genius of Spanish stress: HAB-lo (stress on first syllable, no accent) means 'I speak' (present). ha-BLÓ (stress on final ó, with an accent) means 'he/she/usted spoke' (past)! Never treat the written accent mark in the preterite as optional — it carries the entire tense!
pattern.linguist_note: Latin perfecthabuī/amāvī contracted into -é/-aste/-ó/-amos/-aron in Castilian.
pattern.trap_note: Notice that fue (one syllable) has NO accent mark because one-syllable words in Spanish don't need an accent to show which syllable is stressed!

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:

matching_pairs.english: it was / he went (shared preterite of ser & ir!)
I speak (present, no accent) vs he spoke (past, accented)

exercises.target_answer: hablé, comí, fue, ayer, hablo vs habló
exercises.meaning: I spoke (yesterday), I ate (yesterday), it was / he went (shared preterite of ser & ir!), yesterday, I speak (present, no accent) vs he spoke (past, accented)
exercises.explanation: -ar preterite: -é / -ó; -er/-ir preterite: -í / -ió; ser & ir share fue.

exercises.prompt: What is the difference between 'hablo' (no accent) and 'habló' (with an acute accent)?
exercises.explanation: Without the accent, stress falls on HAB-lo ('I speak'); with the accent, stress jumps to ha-BLÓ ('he/she spoke')!

exercises.prompt: Assemble: 'Yesterday I spoke with my mother'
exercises.meaning: Yesterday I spoke with my mother
exercises.explanation: Ayer ('Yesterday' — closed past dot) triggers the preterite hablé.

exercises.idea: say that yesterday you ate at this restaurant
cues: at/in this restaurant → en este restaurante
idea_parts: at this restaurant → en este restaurante
exercises.meaning: Yesterday I ate at this restaurant
exercises.explanation: Ayer comí en este restaurante — comí is the 1st-person preterite of comer.

diagnosis.slip: used como or he comido with Ayer
diagnosis.cue: With closed past markers like ayer ('yesterday'), use the one-word preterite: Ayer comí.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: a fantastic day: un día fantástico
exercises.explanation: Ayer fue un día fantástico — fue is the 3rd-person preterite of both ser and ir!

summary.outcome: Express completed past events with -ar (-é/-ó) and -er/-ir (-í/-ió) preterite forms and fue.

use_example.german: Ayer hablé con mi amigo y comí en el restaurante.
use_example.english: Yesterday I spoke with my friend and ate at the restaurant.

summary.takeaway: In the preterite, the written accent on -é, -ó, -í, -ió is the engine of the past tense.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next ([1801] -ar Preterite Endings): master the -ar preterite paradigm and why nosotros (hablamos) uses context to show tense.

foreshadow.line: If the Preterite is a snapshot dot in time ('yesterday I spoke'), how do you paint an ongoing video background in the past ('I was speaking, I used to live')? Topic 19 unveils the Imperfect!

payoff.text: Compare Topic 17 (Hoy he hablado 'Today I have spoken' — open time window) with Topic 18 (Ayer hablé 'Yesterday I spoke' — closed dot in time).

hablé.context_translation: Yesterday I spoke with my mother.
hablé.etymology_derivation: Notice how the accent mark carries the entire tense difference: hablo ('I speak') vs. habló ('he/she spoke')!

comí.context_translation: Yesterday I ate at that restaurant.

fue.english_cognate: was / went (shared preterite of ser & ir!)
fue.shift_rule: Shared preterite of ser and ir (fui, fuiste, fue)
fue.etymology_derivation: ser ('to be') and ir ('to go') share the exact same preterite forms: fui ('I was / I went'), fue ('it was / he went')!

visitar.etymology_derivation: visitation → visitar. No preposition 'to' needed in Spanish: quiero visitar (two words where English needs three).

celebrar.etymology_derivation: celebración → celebrar. The trap: not *celebratar. Strip the whole -ación before adding -ar.

comer.etymology_derivation: Latin com- ('completely') + edere ('to eat', cousin of English edible and eat).

vivir.etymology_derivation: Latin vīvere — English vivid, revive, survive.

ser.etymology_derivation: Ser describes what something is: identity, origin, inherent nature. Latin esse fused with sedēre ('to sit/settle').

ir.context_translation: I am going to go tomorrow.
ir.etymology_derivation: Latin īre ('to go', preserved in English exit 'go out' and transit 'go across')!
